body:
emily-support: Heads-up: John (acct: acct_8899) opened a ticket — says their promo/free credits dropped to 0 while Console showed 5 remaining. They did not receive any expiry email and insist usage hasn't changed.

john-customer: I just checked, dashboard still shows 5 free credits but my invoice is full price. Please advise.

sam-billing: Can you paste invoice id + acct? I'll reconcile ledger rows.

emily-support: Invoice: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-2026-11-4420
Account: acct_8899
Attached screenshot shows Console: "Free credits: 5" and the billing email showing charges.

mike-platform: Quick suspicion: are they primarily using embeddings or streaming generation? Our Console widget reports promo units, which can lag; ledger records token-equivalent after conversion. If they switched to batched embedding calls, conversion could exhaust credits faster than UI shows.

john-customer: We started a batch embed job and also had a client reconnect loop from our side (socket reconnect) around 2026-11-14 01:12 UTC. We didn't expect retries to be billed multiple times.

nina-eng: If client-side reconnects triggered full replays, ingress counts each complete request. We also had a known partial-window caching inconsistency last quarter where promo_balance cache TTL could be stale up to ~45m under certain cache-pop churn.

sam-billing: Pulling ledger now... Invoice INV-2026-11-4420 processed 2026-11-15T04:08:22Z — tokens billed: 432,100 — promo credits applied: 0. There is an earlier auto-conversion record at 2026-11-14T01:20:00Z that converted embed units to token-equivalents and consumed the promo bucket before the Console cache refreshed.

emily-support: Customer attached a sanitized request bundle showing repeated req_ids and identical payloads. Uploaded to s3: s3://support-uploads/189001122/trace.tar.gz

mike-platform: Looking at ingress logs for acct_8899 — I see a sequence of identical requests with different transient req_ids from 01:11:30 to 01:13:05 UTC. The client resumed playback on websocket reconnect and re-sent batches. Each one produced a usage event. Also saw a spike in embed.batch calls which use a 1:token conversion we currently apply during billing ingestion.

nina-eng: Repro query for events (use to confirm duplicates):
```
SELECT req_id, count(*) FROM ingress.events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_8899'
AND ts BETWEEN '2026-11-14T01:10:00Z' AND '2026-11-14T01:20:00Z'
GROUP BY req_id
HAVING count(*) > 1;
```
If rows returned, ingress duplicated receipts. Also verify streaming partials didn't emit final token counts until full completion.

sam-billing: That aligns — ledger shows the conversion and billing happened before cache invalidation. Console pulled promo_balance from cache (TTL ~45m) and displayed 5 while ledger already consumed them. So root cause looks like: client reconnect/retries caused duplicate usage events + cache/ledger race window. Not a promo burn ordering bug per se.

john-customer: We rely on Console to know how many free credits remain. How can we avoid surprises?

emily-support: Immediate plan: offer temporary goodwill credit to offset unexpected charges and explain root cause. Engineering will harden ingress dedupe and tighten cache freshness alerts.

sam-billing: I'll create a billing adjustment now for 200 credits as a one-time goodwill (ADJ-2026-6012). Will note for reconciliation and postmortem.

billing-bot: Adjustment ADJ-2026-6012 created for acct_8899 
status: pending_reconciliation

nina-eng: Proposed technical mitigations:
- Add a dedupe layer in ingress to collapse repeated requests with same client nonce/trace within a 60s window and emit a single usage event.
- Add an indicator metric for promo_balance_cache_age and alert >300s.
- Ensure embed.batch conversion is idempotent (attach conversion id to usage events).

mike-platform: Low-risk change to ingress: collapse by client_nonce and path for 60s behind a feature flag. I'll add a metric `ingress.dedupe.hits` and a dashboard graph. Also will add a conditional log when billing conversion fires for embed.batch.

emily-support: Draft message to John (ready to send):
"Hi John 
Thanks for raising this. We investigated and found a burst of replayed requests from your client during a websocket reconnect that resulted in duplicated usage events. Meanwhile our Console read a cached promo balance that had not yet reflected the ledger consumption, so the UI showed 5 credits while billing had already used them. We've applied a one-time 200-credit goodwill adjustment (ADJ-2026-6012) while we harden our metering. We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline for the fix. Apologies for the confusion. 
— Emily (Support)"

john-customer: Thanks, appreciate the quick response. Please let me know when the dedupe change is live.

sam-billing: Message sent to customer 2026-11-15T09:30Z. Adjustment ADJ-2026-6012 is in pending_reconciliation.

nina-eng: Created ticket ENG-4720 to implement ingress dedupe and cache-age alerts. Tagging billing and support owners for postmortem.

mike-platform: I'll ship the dedupe flag to staging today and schedule rollout to prod after load tests. Also setting alert for promo_balance_cache_age > 300s.

billing-bot: ADJ-2026-6012 status updated: applied_to_account (pending invoice reconciliation).

emily-support: Customer replied: "OK thanks, that clarifies it. We'll watch for the prod rollout." :thumbsup:

sam-billing: Closing this escalation thread for now; will reopen if reconciliation shows any remaining mismatch. Linking ENG-4720 in the customer ticket and adding a short billing postmortem doc.

emily-support: Closing thread and leaving detailed note on the account. Thanks everyone.
